source.title: Generalization Ability of Wide Neural Networks on ℝ
source.authors: Jian-Fa Lai; Manyun Xu; R. Chen; Qi-Rong Lin

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The authors’ own theoretical result says that, in their equally spaced one-dimensional regression setting, a sufficiently trained overfitted network retains a constant lower bound on excess risk, contrary to the late improvement predicted by epoch-wise double descent. Their experiments also examine how signal strength and label corruption affect training-time behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper does not sweep model size or sample size to measure test error. Figure 1 compares interpolation forms at different widths, not test error, so it is not a model-wise double-descent result. The paper’s experiments on stopping times and label corruption are shown in figures without tabulated values; their reported outcomes concern stopping-time gaps and signal strength, not an explicitly described fall-rise-fall test-error curve. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper never studies double descent. It cites Nakkiran et al. only as one of several 'benign overfitting' experiments. Its results compare an early-stopped wide two-layer ReLU network (minimax rate n^-2/3) with a network trained long enough to interpolate. On equally spaced 1D data, the interpolating network has excess risk above a positive constant. Neither theorem describes the test-error trajectory between these two points, so nothing shows whether a fall-rise-fall shape exists. A constant lower bound on the final risk does not rule out a second descent. The construct is benign overfitting and interpolation consistency, not double descent. The synthetic and CIFAR-10 experiments measure the gap between the 100%-label-accuracy time and the optimal stopping time against label corruption. Their test-loss curves are figure-only and the text never describes their shape.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors prove that NNK converges uniformly to NTK. Under their assumptions, an early-stopped wide network is minimax optimal, while an overfitted one on equally spaced 1D data is nearly a linear interpolant and cannot generalize. They reconcile this with benign overfitting by hypothesising implicit early stopping at 100% label accuracy. That stopping time lies near the optimal time when signal is strong and near the loss-overfitting time when signal is weak.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies gradient-flow training of wide two-layer ReLU networks through NTK regression and early stopping; it does not reproduce a double-descent size or sample sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported stopping-time/generalization behavior is described as depending on signal strength, represented in the experiments by label-corruption probability; the gap between tlabel and topt increases as corruption increases.

fits_no_version.finding: In the NTK regime on equally spaced 1D data, a wide two-layer ReLU network trained past t > C1 n^2 log n is nearly a linear interpolant. Its excess risk stays above a constant depending on σ, while early stopping at t ∝ n^(2/3) attains the n^-2/3 minimax rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolating wide networks in the lazy regime are inconsistent in low dimension (benign overfitting fails); only early stopping generalizes optimally.

fits_no_version.finding: The gap between the 100%-label-accuracy stopping time and the optimal stopping time grows with label corruption (p=0, 0.3, 0.6). This holds for synthetic data with squared or cross-entropy loss and for AlexNet on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Apparent benign overfitting reflects implicit early stopping at label-accuracy time, which nears the optimal time only when signal strength is high.

record.peer_reviewed: preprint; submitted to the Annals of Statistics (review status not stated)
record.problems: The main theoretical generalization results rely on stated assumptions, including an RKHS condition, and the poor-generalization result is for equally spaced one-dimensional data. The experiments do not provide tabulated curve values or uncertainty estimates; the synthetic experiment uses 100 training samples and 1000 test points, and the text does not state the CIFAR-10 sample counts.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1's varying-width interpolation plots are excluded because they do not report test error. No other claim-relevant outcomes are omitted.

untested.parts: The test-error shape over training time is not described in text. The only theoretical results are the early-stopped and fully trained endpoints.
No model-size sweep of test error.
No sample-size sweep near the interpolation threshold.
Label corruption is varied, but no test-error peak is measured against it.

missing.what: Testing-loss curves over training time at p=0, 0.3, 0.6. If they show a rise-then-fall, they could bear on V2 (and on label-noise dependence, V6), but the text gives no description or values.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T5 and 'challenges V2' verdict over-read Theorem 4.2(ii). A constant lower bound on the final interpolant's excess risk says nothing about whether test error rises and then falls again during training. The paper frames its results against benign overfitting, not double descent. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep of test error or test-error peak near the interpolation threshold.

The paper does not report a complete numerical fall-rise-fall curve over training time; its theoretical comparison is between a properly early-stopped predictor and sufficiently late overfitting, and its experimental curves are figure-only.
No comparison of test error across training-sample sizes near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes testing a general double-descent curve.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak locations across axes.

Label corruption and signal strength are examined, but the paper does not test whether noise drives a double-descent peak, whether peaks split, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes a peak.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameters or test of whether that converts a second descent into a U shape.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Overfitting the equally spaced one-dimensional regression data with a sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU network
reader_labels.reason: Theorem 4.2(ii) gives a positive constant lower bound on excess risk after t > C1 n^2 log n, so the predicted late improvement is absent in this setting (R2). The early-stopping bound in R1 supplies a comparison point but not a full curve.
